the expression of VIP and its receptors increases during malignant transformation in human prostate gland, and that VIP and VIP receptors are functional in both normal and malignant tissues.
the VIP system is differentially expressed in normal and malignant human prostate, and that VIP antagonistic action of the GHRH analog JV-1-33 may be used in prostate cancer therapy.
VIP is expressed in human normal prostate and in prostate carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression and function of VIP and its receptors in human prostate and in prostate cancer.
the study of the expression and functionality of VIP and VIP receptor subtypes in normal and malignant prostate tissue.
the identification of the VIP receptors and their function in the prostate gland and prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VIP is a growth factor in the prostate gland acting by paracrine/autocrine mechanisms.
VIP is expressed at higher levels in human prostate cancer and that the expression of VPAC1, VPAC2, and PAC1 receptors is also higher in prostate cancer than normal prostate.
the expression of VIP and its receptors is increased during malignant transformation of the prostate gland.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VIP and VIP analogs could be considered for the treatment of prostate cancer.
the VIP system (VIP, VPAC1, VPAC2 and PAC1) is expressed in normal and malignant prostates, with the highest expression levels in cancer tissue.
the VIP system is overexpressed in prostate cancer and the peptide may be used as a diagnostic marker or therapeutic target.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VIP receptors are over-expressed in prostate cancer, and that the GHRH analog JV-1-35 is a VIP antagonist in prostate tissue.
VIP and its receptors play a role in the development of human prostate cancer, and that a VIP antagonist (e.g., JV-1- 53) may prove to be useful as a therapeutic tool for prostate cancer.
VIP and GHRH analogs can be useful in the management of human prostatic cancer, either alone or in combination with other agents.
